stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
passage: After spending nearly fourteen months analyzing sediment cores extracted from Lake Malawi_______ geochemist Dr. Farai Moyo published a study revealing that the lake's phosphorus concentrations had fluctuated dramatically over the past eight centuries.
explanation: The sentence begins with a dependent adverbial phrase introduced by "After," which must be followed by a comma before the main clause. The option placing a comma after "Malawi" correctly sets off the introductory dependent phrase from the independent clause that follows. A period after "Malawi" is incorrect because it would leave "After spending nearly fourteen months analyzing sediment cores extracted from Lake Malawi" as a sentence fragment, since it lacks a main verb and cannot stand alone. A semicolon is incorrect because it requires independent clauses on both sides, but the opening phrase beginning with "After" is dependent, not independent. Omitting punctuation entirely produces a run-together construction that violates standard conventions for setting off introductory elements.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
passage: The Horyuji temple complex in Nara Prefecture contains some of the oldest surviving wooden structures in the world_______ architectural historians have long debated whether the original builders used a form of earthquake-resistant joinery that predates modern seismic engineering by over a millennium.
explanation: Two independent clauses appear on either side of the blank: "The Horyuji temple complex in Nara Prefecture contains some of the oldest surviving wooden structures in the world" and "architectural historians have long debated whether the original builders used a form of earthquake-resistant joinery." A semicolon correctly joins two closely related independent clauses without a coordinating conjunction. A comma alone between the two independent clauses creates a comma splice, which is a grammatical error in Standard English. Omitting punctuation entirely produces a run-on sentence, fusing two independent clauses with no separation. The option using a period followed by "The structures, they" introduces a double subject: both "The structures" and "they" serve as the subject of the same clause, producing a nonstandard construction.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
passage: The restoration of the Uffizi Gallery's fifteenth-century altarpiece took an unexpected turn when conservators discovered, beneath layers of later overpainting_______ a portrait that bore no resemblance to the figure depicted in the visible composition and that appeared to predate the altarpiece itself by at least forty years.
explanation: The phrase "beneath layers of later overpainting" is a parenthetical modifier inserted between the verb "discovered" and its direct object "a portrait." Because this parenthetical was opened with a comma before "beneath," it must be closed with a matching comma after "overpainting" to complete the pair. The option placing a comma after "overpainting" correctly closes the parenthetical and allows the sentence to continue to the direct object. A semicolon is incorrect because there are not two independent clauses on either side of the blank; "a portrait that bore no resemblance..." is a noun phrase serving as the direct object, not an independent clause. Omitting punctuation leaves the opening comma before "beneath" unpaired and produces a construction that obscures the relationship between "discovered" and its object "a portrait." A period after "overpainting" would leave "A portrait that bore no resemblance to the figure depicted in the visible composition and that appeared to predate the altarpiece itself by at least forty years" as a sentence fragment, since it consists of a noun phrase with relative clauses but no main verb.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
passage: The collection of rare jade figurines displayed in the Taipei National Palace Museum_______ visitors from around the world who are drawn to the intricate craftsmanship of Qing dynasty artisans.
explanation: The subject of the sentence is "collection," a singular noun. The intervening prepositional phrase "of rare jade figurines" and the participial phrase "displayed in the Taipei National Palace Museum" do not change the number of the subject. A singular subject requires a singular verb form. The option "attracts" correctly provides a third-person singular present-tense verb consistent with a general statement of fact. The bare plural form "attract" does not agree with the singular subject "collection." The present-perfect plural "have attracted" incorrectly treats "figurines" as the subject and shifts the tense. The present-progressive plural "are attracting" also fails to agree with the singular "collection" and implies a temporary ongoing action rather than a habitual one.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
passage: Neither the lead archaeologist nor her three graduate assistants_______ able to explain why the burial site contained fragments of obsidian that could only have originated from a volcanic deposit more than two thousand kilometers away.
explanation: In a "neither...nor" construction, the verb agrees in number with the subject closer to it. Here, "her three graduate assistants" is the nearer subject and is plural, so the verb must also be plural. The option "were" correctly provides a plural past-tense verb agreeing with "assistants." The singular past-tense "was" incorrectly treats "the lead archaeologist" as the governing subject for agreement. The singular present-perfect "has been" fails on both number (singular rather than plural) and tense (present perfect rather than simple past, inconsistent with the past-tense "contained" in the clause that follows). The singular present-tense "is" fails on both number and tense for the same reasons.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
passage: By the time the Chilean observatory's adaptive optics system completed its final calibration in March 2024, astronomer Dr. Lucia Herrera_______ the same binary star system for eleven consecutive years, amassing a dataset that would later reshape models of stellar evolution in low-metallicity environments.
explanation: The construction "By the time [past-tense event]" signals that another action was ongoing up to and before that past event, requiring the past perfect progressive tense. The duration marker "for eleven consecutive years" further confirms that the action was continuous over an extended period leading up to the calibration. The option "had been studying" correctly places the ongoing study before the past reference point of the calibration's completion. The simple past "studied" fails to establish the required temporal sequence showing an action in progress before another past event and does not pair correctly with the "by the time" construction. The present-perfect progressive "has been studying" anchors the action to the present moment, which conflicts with the entirely past-tense narrative. The conditional "would study" implies a hypothetical or planned future action, contradicting the passage's indication that the observation was a completed, ongoing endeavor.
